takeoff_ground_roll_provenance.title: Normal Takeoff Distance
takeoff_ground_roll_provenance.conditions: Full throttle and 2700 RPM before brake release, mixtures leaned for field elevation, wing flaps up, cowl flaps open, level hard surface dry runway
notes: If full power is applied without brakes set, distances apply from the point where full power is applied.
Decrease distance 7% for each 10 knots headwind.
Increase distance 5% for each 2 knots tailwind.
Increase total distance 7.9% for operation on a firm dry sod runway.
Takeoff speed to the 50 foot obstacle: 92 KIAS at 5500 lb, 88 KIAS at 5100 lb, 85 KIAS at 4700 lb, 81 KIAS at 4300 lb.

These are the 20, 30 and 40 degree C columns, which are sheet 2 of the figure. Sheet 1 (printed page 5-22, PDF page 132) prints -20, -10, 0 and 10 degree C for the same four weights and eleven altitudes and is not carried here.

The 5500 lb block stops at 9000 ft. The handbook prints a 10,000 ft row for it (5410/7640 at 20 C, 5880/8720 at 30 C, 6390/10,270 at 40 C), but 10,270 is printed with a thousands separator that the extractor's numeric pattern does not accept, which would leave a half-read pair, so that row is clipped out of the sheet rather than published half-read. The other three weights carry their 10,000 ft rows.

landing_ground_roll_provenance.title: Normal Landing Distance
landing_ground_roll_provenance.conditions: Throttles idle, landing gear down, wing flaps 35 deg, cowl flaps closed, level hard surface runway, maximum braking effort
notes: Increase distance by 25% of the ground run for operation on a firm sod runway.
If it is necessary to land with wing flaps up, increase the approach speed 12 knots above the normal approach speed and expect total landing distance to increase by 35%.
Decrease total distances by 3% for each 4 knots headwind. For tailwinds up to 10 knots, increase total distances by 5% for each 2 knots of wind.
Speed at the 50 foot obstacle: 93 KIAS at 5400 lb, 89 KIAS at 5000 lb, 86 KIAS at 4600 lb, 82 KIAS at 4200 lb.
The landing weights stop at 5400 lb because that is the maximum landing weight printed under WEIGHT LIMITS on printed page 2-5 (PDF page 25). 5500 lb is the takeoff limit.

These are the 20, 30 and 40 degree C columns, which are sheet 2 of the figure. Sheet 1 (printed page 5-42, PDF page 152) prints -20, -10, 0 and 10 degree C for the same four weights and eleven altitudes and is not carried here.

rate_of_climb_provenance.title: Rate-of-Climb - Cruise Climb
rate_of_climb_provenance.conditions: 2500 RPM and 24.5 inches Hg, landing gear up, wing flaps up, cowl flaps as required, 120 KIAS, mixtures at the recommended fuel flow. The handbook footnotes this figure "above 5200 feet, use full throttle": below that height the engines are throttled to hold 24.5 inches, so power stays put while drag falls with the air, and the rate of climb RISES with altitude up to about 5000 ft before falling away
notes: Above 5200 feet, use full throttle.

This is the CRUISE climb, at 2500 RPM and 120 KIAS, not the maximum-rate climb. It is the only rate of climb this handbook prints as a table. Rate-of-Climb Maximum Climb (Figure 5-14, printed page 5-28) and Rate-of-Climb Single Engine (Figure 5-16, printed page 5-30) are both carpet charts of curves, so neither can be transcribed here. Cruise climb is the slower of the two, so a climb figure read from this table is never higher than the maximum-climb figure the same handbook publishes.

Rate of climb RISES from sea level to 5000 ft in every column of this table, then falls. That is the aeroplane, not a misread: at a fixed 24.5 inches Hg the engines make more power as exhaust back pressure drops, up to the roughly 5200 ft full-throttle altitude named in the conditions. The extractor's monotonicity check expects a climb table to fall in both axes, so it reports 102 altitude-direction reversals on this figure. All 102 sit in the sea level to 5000 ft band, the temperature direction is clean everywhere, and every cell was checked against the printed page.

stall_speeds_provenance.title: Stall Speeds
stall_speeds_provenance.conditions: Throttles idle, 5500 lb gross weight. Gear up at flaps 0 deg; gear down at flaps 15 deg and 35 deg
notes: Maximum altitude lost during a stall is 300 feet.
Maximum pitch in a power-off stall is 10 deg.

The handbook prints this figure at four weights (5500, 5100, 4700 and 4300 lb) in four blocks under one header. Only the 5500 lb block is carried, because the shared extractor takes a stall sheet's weight from the sheet and only the top block can be clipped together with the header it needs. 5500 lb is maximum gross, so these are the highest stall speeds the figure publishes.

The clip and OCR settings on this sheet are deliberate and tight. The scan's rows slope about 0.6 deg, so a row's eight values span nearly the whole 4 pt band the extractor groups rows into. Reading the sheet in ONE pass (strip_pt wider than the clip) keeps each value to a single token, and the 360 degree rotate is a full turn that changes nothing about the image but makes ocr.py report coordinates relative to the clip, so the clip's top edge at 145.0 sets which 4 pt band each row lands in. Moving that edge by 0.1 pt drops a cell.
